walkthroughs.body_html:
Plant Biology — a core area of Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Plant Biology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Plant Biology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Munch's pressure flow hypothesis for phloem transport dates from:

options: Cytokinin
Auxin (IAA)
Ethylene
Abscisic acid

mcqs.q: Do all arteries carry oxygenated blood?
options: Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.
All arteries carry oxygenated blood and all veins carry deoxygenated blood.
PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
No — the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

mcqs.q: What are the three repeated stages of one PCR cycle?
options: Denaturation (high temp, strands separate), annealing (lower temp, primers bind), extension (Taq polymerase synthesises new strands).
PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.
PCR has just one stage — heating the DNA until it copies itself.

mcqs.q: What makes the antigen-binding site of an antibody specific to one antigen?
options: PCR uses enzymes from bacteria to cut DNA into fragments, then sticks them back together.
Antibodies bind to any antigen they meet first.
The variable region — its amino acid sequence (and thus shape) differs between antibodies, complementing a specific antigen.
All antibodies have the same binding site; specificity comes from where they go in the body.
